prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1022; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a sideswipe that occurred while the insured vehicle was changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant was the driver of the insured vehicle, and the policyholder confirmed the driver is a member of the household and covered under the policy.

Entry 2: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene. The other driver's statement describes the same lane change and contact along the passenger side.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses were reached and both describe the vehicles making contact as one drifted into the adjacent lane. Scene photos were received and show scraping and a dented rear quarter panel consistent with the reported impact.

Entry 4: Claimant reports pain in the right shoulder and was transported to an urgent care facility the same day. Medical records requested and a treating provider has been identified.

Entry 5: Estimate received for the body work. Most of the damage appears to be in line with the described contact, and the appraiser noted nothing that conflicts with the account given so far.

Entry 6: Claimant is now represented by an attorney, who has asked that all further contact go through their office. Recorded the representation and paused direct contact with the claimant.

Entry 7: Treating physician notes describe a shoulder strain with a soft tissue component, which the adjuster considers a reasonable match for the force of a side impact. Treatment has been physical therapy and over-the-counter medication, and the notes show steady improvement.

Entry 8: Attorney's office provided a written account that adds a few small details, such as the exact position of the other vehicle before the lane change. The core sequence of events remains the same as in the original report.

Entry 9: A neighbor contacted the desk and stated the insured vehicle appeared to have body damage several weeks before the reported accident. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file, and the neighbor has not provided photos or other support for the observation.

Entry 10: Reviewed prior claims and medical history databases. No earlier injury to the shoulder or other affected area has been found for the claimant, and the vehicle shows no prior loss on record.

Entry 11: Physical therapy has tapered as the claimant's range of motion has returned, and the treating provider expects discharge from active care soon. File remains open pending final medical bills and the attorney's demand package, with the neighbor's comment noted for follow-up.
